patterns.usage_note: After a dictionary-form verb, 〜までだ／〜までのことだ states a fallback the speaker is calm about: if the preferred route fails, they will simply do this instead, so it usually follows a conditional clause. 〜までのことだ is the emphatic variant. Unlike 〜つもりだ, which reports a plan formed in advance, 〜までだ announces the option left over when the preferred route closes. Do not confuse it with the ta-form 〜たまでだ, which downplays a past act as having no motive beyond the obvious ('I only answered because I was asked').

examples.ruby: 駄目[だめ]なら、また一[いち]からやり直[なお]すまでだ。
examples.english: If it doesn't work out, I'll simply start over from scratch.

examples.ruby: 誰[だれ]も来[こ]ないなら、一人[ひとり]で始[はじ]めるまでのことだ。
examples.english: If nobody shows up, I'll just get started on my own, that's all.

examples.ruby: 今更[いまさら]悔[く]やんでも遅[おそ]い、できることをやるまでだ。
examples.english: It's too late for regrets now; I'll simply do what I can.
